title: Senior's toolkit: collections in practice
summary: The Dictionary, HashSet and List APIs experienced developers reach for, and how to inspect collections in the debugger.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: collections in practice
steps.body: Most real code is moving data between lists, dictionaries and sets. These are the calls that avoid the common crashes and double lookups, and the debugger views that show you what is inside.

toolkit.what: Look a key up once and get a `bool` back, instead of `ContainsKey` followed by `dict[key]` (two lookups) or `dict[key]` alone (which throws `KeyNotFoundException`).
flags: when a default is all you need
toolkit.example:
if (prices.TryGetValue(sku, out var price)) total += price * qty;
else missing.Add(sku);

toolkit.what: Add only if the key is new, and get `false` instead of an `ArgumentException` when it already exists.
flags: throws if the key exists: use it when a duplicate is a bug
keep the first value and tell me

toolkit.what: Pass a comparer so `"Urgent"` and `"urgent"` are the same key. Works the same for `Dictionary<string, T>`.
flags: case-insensitive, culture-independent: right for ids, tags, emails
only for text shown to people

toolkit.what: Count or update a dictionary entry with one lookup, in hot loops. It returns a reference to the value slot, adding the key if needed. In `System.Runtime.InteropServices`.
flags: increment the stored value in place
tells you whether the key was already there
other keys while holding the reference
toolkit.example:
foreach (var word in words)
    CollectionsMarshal.GetValueRefOrAddDefault(counts, word, out _)++;
toolkit.when: a profiler shows dictionary lookups in a tight loop; otherwise TryGetValue is clearer

toolkit.what: Collection expressions build a list, array or span in one line, and `..` spreads another collection into it.
flags: an empty collection of the target type

toolkit.cmd: Debugger: hover, Results View and the table visualizer
toolkit.what: Hover a list or dictionary to see its `Count` and items. In Visual Studio the magnifier next to a collection opens a table you can sort and filter.
flags: the real fields inside the collection
(Visual Studio) IEnumerable visualizer: items as a table
toolkit.example: Stop after the loop, hover `counts`, expand it

steps.prompt: The nightly import crashes with this. Which change fixes it properly?
code: Unhandled exception. System.Collections.Generic.KeyNotFoundException: The given key 'SKU-9912' was not present in the dictionary.
options: Use `prices.TryGetValue(line.Sku, out var price)` and send the unknown SKU to an error list
Wrap line 41 in `try { } catch { }` and carry on
Call `prices.ContainsKey(line.Sku)` first and then `prices[line.Sku]` inside a `try`
Switch the `Dictionary` to a `List` and search it
steps.explain: A missing key is an expected case in imported data, so handle it with `TryGetValue`: one lookup, no exception, and the unknown SKU is recorded instead of hidden.
`GetValueOrDefault` gives `0` for a missing `int`. `TryAdd` refuses the existing key and leaves 3 in place. The comparer makes the three spellings of Urgent one item.

steps.prompt: Match each call to what happens when the key already exists.
pairs: keeps the old value, returns false
returns true and puts the value in x

steps.prompt: Count words in one lookup per word, case-insensitively.
steps.explain: `GetValueRefOrAddDefault` returns a reference to the slot (0 for a new key), so `++` updates the dictionary directly. `GetValueOrDefault` and `TryGetValue` are methods of the dictionary itself and hand back a copy of the value, so they cannot update it in place.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Whenever you write `dict[key]` on data that came from outside, ask what happens if the key is missing, and reach for `TryGetValue`. Pick the string comparer on purpose every time you key by text. Hover collections in the debugger instead of printing them.
